questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following methods is best suited for the preparation of methylamine from acetamide?
questions.explanation: Hofmann bromamide degradation (treating amide with Br2 and NaOH) converts acetamide (CH3CONH2) to methylamine (CH3NH2), losing one carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which statement is CORRECT regarding the basicity of amines?
options: Aliphatic amines are weaker bases than ammonia
Aniline is a stronger base than methylamine
Electron-withdrawing groups on the ring decrease the basicity of aryl amines
Increased alkyl substitution always increases basicity in aqueous solution
questions.explanation: Electron-withdrawing groups (like -NO2, -CN) on the benzene ring further delocalize or withdraw the nitrogen lone pair, reducing basicity of the aromatic amine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is a secondary amine?
questions.explanation: A secondary amine has two organic groups attached to nitrogen. (CH3)2NH (dimethylamine) or CH3NHCH3 has exactly two methyl groups, making it a secondary amine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: N-methyl aniline is a:
questions.explanation: N-methylaniline (C6H5-NH-CH3) has nitrogen bonded to two organic groups (phenyl and methyl), making it a secondary amine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The order of basicity in gas phase for amines is:
questions.explanation: In the gas phase, basicity depends purely on electron density at nitrogen. Increasing alkyl substitution increases electron density, so (CH3)3N > (CH3)2NH > CH3NH2 > NH3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Aniline reacting with bromine water gives a white precipitate of:
questions.explanation: The -NH2 group is a powerful activating group and directs electrophilic substitution to all three ortho and para positions. Aniline reacts with Br2/H2O to give 2,4,6-tribromoaniline immediately.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Diazotization of aniline requires the temperature to be maintained at 0-5°C. This is because at higher temperatures:
options: Aniline does not dissolve in HCl
The diazonium salt decomposes to give phenol
The product becomes a secondary amine
questions.explanation: Benzenediazonium chloride is unstable and decomposes at temperatures above 5°C to give phenol and N2 gas. The reaction is maintained at 0-5°C to preserve the product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Reduction of benzene diazonium chloride with H3PO2 (hypophosphorous acid) gives:
questions.explanation: H3PO2 is used to replace the diazonium group (-N2+) with hydrogen (deamination), yielding benzene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct mechanism of Hofmann bromamide reaction?
questions.explanation: The Hofmann bromamide reaction proceeds via formation of an isocyanate intermediate through nitrene rearrangement, ultimately giving a primary amine with one less carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which is the IUPAC name for C6H5-N2+Cl-?
questions.explanation: The IUPAC-accepted name for C6H5N2+Cl- is benzenediazonium chloride, where benzene is the parent ring and diazonium indicates the -N2+ group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The Schiemann reaction converts a diazonium salt to:
questions.explanation: In the Schiemann (Balz-Schiemann) reaction, a diazonium tetrafluoroborate is thermally decomposed to give an aryl fluoride (ArF).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Among the following, which amine will have the highest water solubility?
questions.explanation: Smaller amines are more soluble in water due to effective hydrogen bonding. Methylamine is the smallest amine and is highly soluble in water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The reaction of diazonium fluoroborate with KI gives:
questions.explanation: Aryl iodides cannot be prepared by direct halogenation. Instead, diazonium salt reacts with KI or HI to give aryl iodide (ArI).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about amines is INCORRECT?
options: Amines are basic in nature due to lone pair on nitrogen
Primary amines have higher boiling points than secondary amines of similar molecular weight
Aniline is a stronger base than p-nitroaniline
Tertiary amines cannot form hydrogen bonds with themselves
questions.explanation: Primary amines can form more hydrogen bonds than secondary amines due to having two N-H bonds (vs one in secondary), giving them higher boiling points is TRUE. Actually, this is correct, so the INCORRECT statement is A - the statement is all correct. Wait: The incorrect one here is option B since primary amines (two N-H bonds) do have higher boiling points than secondary amines of comparable molecular weight.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Acetylation of aniline using acetic anhydride yields:
questions.explanation: Aniline reacts with acetic anhydride (CH3CO)2O or acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) to form acetanilide (C6H5NHCOCH3), a N-substituted amide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Azo dyes are formed by the coupling of diazonium salts with:
questions.explanation: Diazonium salts undergo electrophilic coupling with electron-rich aromatic compounds like phenols and aromatic amines to form brightly colored azo dyes (-N=N-).
